# sdocs — full reference

> sdocs is a documentation tool for Svelte 5 components. It renders `.sdoc`
> files into a documentation site: a `.sdoc` file is a documentation format that
> *contains* Svelte — the file's structure is sdoc, and Svelte lives inside
> designated blocks. This is a complete, self-contained reference — setup,
> configuration, the CLI/build, and the full `.sdoc` authoring format — for
> developers and coding assistants. Live docs: https://gabilungu.github.io/sdocs/

## Requirements

- Svelte 5
- Vite with `@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte`

## Setup

Install into a Svelte 5 project:

```bash
npm install sdocs
```

Or skip installing entirely — with `.sdoc` files present, `npx sdocs run`
fetches sdocs into the npx cache and serves them, resolving your components'
dependencies (and your project's own `svelte`) from the project.

Scaffold a config (optional — the defaults work with zero config):

```bash
npx sdocs init
```

This writes `sdocs.config.js` with every option present but commented out.

Write a first doc next to a component (`src/lib/Button.svelte` →
`src/lib/Button.sdoc`):

```sdoc
<script lang="ts">
	import Button from './Button.svelte';
</script>

[SHOWCASE title="Components / Button" description="A flexible button."]

	[component component={Button} args={{ label: 'Click me', disabled: false }}]
		<Button {...args} />
	[/component]

[/SHOWCASE]
```

Run it:

```bash
npx sdocs dev      # dev server at http://localhost:3000
```

## CLI / building

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `npx sdocs init` | Scaffold `sdocs.config.js` (no-op if one exists) |
| `npx sdocs dev` | Dev server with live reload (default port 3000) |
| `npx sdocs run` | Same as `dev`, but works without installing sdocs |
| `npx sdocs build` | Build a static site to `dist/` |
| `npx sdocs preview` | Serve the built `dist/` locally |
| `npx sdocs check` | Compile every doc stage and report what breaks (exits 1 on error) |
| `npx sdocs coverage` | Report which components have a `[component]` preview |
| `npx sdocs mcp` | Serve the sdocs MCP server on stdio (authoring tools for agents) |

Global flags: `--version`/`-v`, `--help`/`-h` — recognised anywhere in the
arguments, and they never run the command (`sdocs build --help` prints help
and writes nothing). All commands read
`sdocs.config.js` (or `.ts`/`.mjs`) from the current directory; the config is
read once at startup, so **restart the dev server after editing it**.

`sdocs dev` watches the `.sdoc` files matching `include` and each documented
component's source, reloading on change.

`sdocs build` prerenders every route to a real `index.html` (with a per-route
`<title>` and meta description) that hydrates on load, plus a `404.html`
fallback — deep links work with no rewrite rules on any static host (GitHub
Pages, Netlify, Vercel, S3). Site-structure errors (unknown `@section`, two
entities on one route, unresolvable `home`) fail the build. Pass `--base` when
serving under a sub-path (a GitHub *project* Pages site lives at `/<repo>/`):

```bash
npx sdocs build --base "/my-repo/"
```

`sdocs check` compiles every stage without starting a server or writing a
build, printing each problem with its file, entity, and stage, and exiting 1
when anything errors — the CI gate for "do all the docs still work?". The MCP
`check_docs` tool runs the same check.

Because `run`/`build` need no local install, CI can build a docs site from a
project that doesn't even depend on sdocs: `npx --yes sdocs build` then publish
`dist/`.

**Embedding** — instead of the standalone server, mount sdocs as a route in an
existing Vite/SvelteKit app via its Vite plugin (`sdocsPlugin()`); options
passed there override the config file, and `routing` defaults to `'hash'` when
embedded.

## MCP server

sdocs ships an MCP server with authoring tools, so an agent can validate and
scaffold `.sdoc` files against the real parser instead of guessing — and read
the current project's components and docs through the same extraction the
Explorer uses:

- `validate_sdoc { source }` — parse `.sdoc` text, return diagnostics
  (message, code, 1-based line/column) and the entities found.
- `scaffold_component_doc { componentPath, title? }` — extract a `.svelte`
  component's props and return a starter `.sdoc` (control defaults derived
  from the props) plus the suggested file path; it never writes files.
- `get_authoring_guide {}` — this guide. Also exposed as the
  `sdocs://authoring-guide` resource.
- `list_docs {}` — map the project's documentation: every `.sdoc` file the
  config's `include` globs match, each with its entities (kind, title), the
  **route** each one serves at (plus a route per example), and the components
  its previews document. The routes come from the Explorer's own router, so
  they're exactly what the site serves — drive a browser over them to smoke
  test every page.
- `check_docs { file? }` — **compile** every stage (previews, examples, page
  and layout bodies) the way the dev server does and report what breaks:
  Svelte compile errors, relative imports that resolve to no file, and grammar
  diagnostics — with the file, entity, stage, and a `.sdoc` line where it maps
  cleanly. `validate_sdoc` only checks the grammar; this catches what
  otherwise appears only when the route is opened. Omit `file` to check the
  whole project. It does not type-check and cannot see runtime-only failures.
- `check_coverage {}` — documentation coverage: which components under the
  `components` globs have a `[component]` preview and which don't, plus
  components documented from more than one file, references that resolve to
  no source, and documented components outside the globs. A compound family
  is measured per sub-component.
- `get_component_api { componentPath }` — a component's full extracted API:
  props (types, defaults, descriptions), events, snippets, methods, states,
  CSS custom properties, and class/rest forwarding.

Two ways to connect:

- **stdio** — `npx sdocs mcp` (e.g. `claude mcp add sdocs -- npx -y sdocs mcp`,
  or the equivalent stdio entry in any MCP client config). The VS Code sdocs
  extension registers this server automatically.
- **HTTP** — while `sdocs dev` runs, the same server is served at
  `http://localhost:3000/mcp` (stateless streamable HTTP, POST), and the
  Explorer top bar shows an **MCP** button with the connection info. Dev only:
  built sites are static and carry no MCP endpoint. Disable both with
  `mcp: false` in `sdocs.config.js` (the explicit `sdocs mcp` command still
  works).

## Configuration

sdocs reads `sdocs.config.js` (or `.ts`/`.mjs`) from the project root — checked
in the order `.ts` → `.mjs` → `.js`, first found wins (prefer `.js`/`.mjs`
unless your Node strips TS types). Missing config is fine; defaults apply.

```ts
interface SdocsConfig {
	include?: string | string[];        // globs for .sdoc files. Default ['./src/**/*.sdoc']
	port?: number;                       // dev port. Default 3000 (standalone CLI only)
	open?: boolean;                      // open the browser on dev/preview. Default false
	css?: string | Record<string, string>; // stylesheet(s) loaded into STAGES only. Default null
	title?: string;                      // top-bar title. Default 'sdocs'
	logo?: string | false;               // 'sdocs' mascot | image URL | false. Default 'sdocs'
	favicon?: string;                    // tab icon path/URL
	sections?: { slug: string; title?: string; order?: string[] }[];
	home?: string;                       // route path of the landing page
	routing?: 'history' | 'hash';        // Default 'history' (CLI), 'hash' (embedded)
	base?: string;                       // public base path for build. Default '/'
	mcp?: boolean;                       // serve /mcp + the top-bar MCP button in dev. Default true
	components?: string | string[];      // component globs for coverage. Default: include with .sdoc → .svelte
	static?: string;                     // static assets folder, served at site root
	content?: {                          // per-entity-kind sizing/stage defaults (see below)
		doc?:      { maxWidth?: string; padding?: string; toc?: boolean; contentX?: string };
		page?:     { maxWidth?: string; padding?: string; contentX?: string };
		showcase?: { maxWidth?: string; padding?: string; direction?: string; gap?: string; contentX?: string; contentY?: string; background?: string; minHeight?: string };
		layout?:   { maxWidth?: string; padding?: string; background?: string; minHeight?: string };
	};
}
```

Key options:

- **`include`** — glob(s) matching `.sdoc` files. Relative to project root.
- **`css`** — stylesheet(s) loaded into **stages only** (preview/example iframes
  and `[LAYOUT]` pages), never page prose or the docs chrome — this is what keeps
  "your product" and "the documentation" visually separate. A single path, or a
  `{ name: path }` map the reader switches between via a dropdown (e.g. light /
  dark). Keep build stylesheets self-contained (inline `@import`/`url()`; fonts
  can be data URIs).
- **`static`** — a folder served at the site root in dev and copied into
  `dist/`. In **prose** reference assets root-absolute (`![hero](/hero.png)`);
  inside **stages** reference them **base-relative, no leading slash**
  (`src="hero.png"`, `path="icons/x.svg"`), because the stage carries a
  `<base href>` for correct resolution under a sub-path deploy.
- **`sections`** — the top-bar sections in order, each `{ slug, title?, order? }`.
  `slug` is the first route segment and what titles reference via `@slug/…`;
  `order` is an array of route paths that sort first. Default: a single implicit
  `docs` section. Referencing an undeclared section is a build error.
- **`home`** — route path of the landing page (root URL + logo target). Default:
  the built-in About page. Must resolve to an entity.
- **`base`** — set to `/<repo>/` for a GitHub project Pages deploy (or pass
  `--base` on the CLI). Applies to `build` only.

`content` defaults, overridable per entity/block with the same attributes
(**block beats entity beats config**):

| kind | maxWidth | padding | other |
|---|---|---|---|
| `doc` | `1200px` | `32px` | `toc: true`, `contentX: left` |
| `page` | `1200px` | `32px` | `contentX: left` |
| `showcase` (stages) | `1200px` | `0px` | `direction: row`, `gap: 16px`, `contentX: left`, `contentY: top`, `background`/`minHeight`: none |
| `layout` | `100%` | `0px` | `background`/`minHeight`: none |

`minHeight` reserves room for content that overflows the stage (an open dropdown
or popover) that the auto-sized preview would otherwise clip.

---

# The `.sdoc` format

## File anatomy

Three parts, in this order (only the entities are required):

1. `<script>` — top, optional. Imports and shared values (JS/TS), visible to
   every entity in the file.
2. Entities — the middle. Any mix of `[SHOWCASE]`, `[DOC]`, `[PAGE]`, `[LAYOUT]`.
   Each is its own route and (usually) its own sidebar entry.
3. `<style>` — bottom, optional. CSS available to the file's previews/examples.

Name the file after its main entity (`Button.sdoc`) and put that entity first.
The file `<script>` is shared *source*, not shared *state*: every preview and
example renders isolated, so each gets its own copy of anything mutable.

## Syntax rules

- Tags are line-anchored square brackets, each on its own line: `[SHOWCASE …]`
  opens, `[/SHOWCASE]` closes.
- Entity tags are UPPERCASE (`[SHOWCASE]`, `[DOC]`, `[PAGE]`, `[LAYOUT]`); inner
  blocks are lowercase (`[component]`, `[example]`). Casing is strict.
- Attributes use Svelte syntax: `title="text"` (string), `component={Button}`
  (expression), `args={{ … }}` (expression). Openers may span multiple lines.
- Svelte code is valid only *inside* blocks; body text outside any block is an
  error.

## The four entities

| Entity | Documents | Context |
|---|---|---|
| `[SHOWCASE]` | components — live previews with controls, examples, extracted API | stages: project |
| `[DOC]` | freeform markdown content, auto table of contents | prose: docs |
| `[PAGE]` | a Svelte-built page (landing pages, custom routes) | docs |
| `[LAYOUT]` | a full-page composition of your product, isolated frame | project |

**Project context vs docs context** (the concept that ties the format together):
`[example]`/`[component]` **stages** and `[LAYOUT]` bodies load your project's
`css` — they look like your product. `[DOC]` prose and `[PAGE]` bodies render in
the **docs** context (the docs app's own styling, its CSS variables) — the
project `css` never touches them. Rule of thumb: *prose is docs-styled, stages
are project-styled.*

## Titles place entities: sections, groups, folders

The `title` is a `/`-separated path that builds a three-level navigation
hierarchy:

- **Section** (`@slug/` prefix) — the top-level separation: a **tab in the top
  bar**, declared in `sdocs.config.js` (`sections: [{ slug, title?, order? }]`).
  Each section has its own sidebar tree, and the slug is the first route
  segment. `title="@components/…"`. An undeclared slug is a full-page error;
  a title with no `@` goes to the `docs` section (implicit when no sections
  are declared). Use sections for the site's major areas: Guides vs Components.
- **Group** (`:` prefix on the first segment after the section) — a **bold
  uppercase header** carving the sidebar into areas of similar things
  (`:Layout`, `:Form`, `:Display`). Expanded by default; only the first
  segment can be a group. `title="@components/:Form / Button"`.
- **Folder** (any plain segment) — a **collapsible tree node** that stacks
  entities under it: `title="Foundations / Page 1"`, `"Foundations / Page 2"`
  puts both pages under a Foundations folder. Folders nest
  (`"Forms / Inputs / Text"`), are purely structural (not pages themselves),
  and start collapsed.

Combine all three: `title="@components/:Layout / sdocs / Button"` → the
`components` tab, the **LAYOUT** group, an `sdocs` folder, a Button page.

**How a segment becomes a route slug**: lowercase → strip anything that isn't a
word character, whitespace, or `-` → replace runs of whitespace and `_` with a
single `-`. **CamelCase is not split**, so `IconButton` becomes `iconbutton`,
not `icon-button`. Write the title with a space (`'Icon Button'`) or override
the segment on the opener — `slug="icon-button"` (lowercase letters, digits,
and hyphens only). `list_docs` returns the resolved route for every entity, so
an agent never has to reimplement this.

Two more structural facts:

- A component page with examples becomes its own expandable node with one
  sub-page per example — selecting the component itself shows its docs. A doc
  with several `[component]` previews gets a distinct compound icon.
- `:` groups are always expanded; folders start collapsed.
- **Ordering**: siblings at every level sort alphabetically; pin items first by
  listing their route paths in the section's `order` array
  (`order: ['introduction', 'form/button']`). The page heading and browser tab
  show only the title's **last segment** — the levels above it structure the
  nav, not the page.

## `[SHOWCASE]` — documenting a component

Holds any number of `[component]` previews (live, control-driven) and `[example]`
blocks (frozen, verbatim). Zero previews is valid (examples-only page). Several
previews grow a **tab bar** — made for compound families like `Tabs`/`Tab` (wrap
the child in its parent inside each preview body).

Attributes: `title` (required), `description` (inline markdown), `slug`, `hide`
(routable but unlisted), plus stage defaults its blocks inherit: `maxWidth`,
`padding`, `direction`, `gap`, `contentX`, `contentY`, `background`.

### `[component]` — a live, interactive preview

```sdoc
[component component={Button} args={{ variant: 'primary', disabled: false }}]
	<Button {...args} />
[/component]
```

- `component={X}` (required) — an identifier imported in a `<script>`. Drives
  prop extraction and the interactive controls. Compound members resolve too —
  `component={NavTree.Item}` from a single `import NavTree from './index.js'`.
- `args={{ … }}` (optional) — this preview's control defaults. In scope in the
  body: spread it (`<X {...args} />`), pick from it, or ignore it.
- `title` (tab label — defaults to the component name; set it to distinguish two
  previews of the same component), `description`, and the same stage attributes.

Declared `args` seed the stage's initial state, so a component that reads a
required prop on first render has it before the controls' first update; a
stage that throws anyway shows the error in place instead of going blank.

**`args` values are plain literals only: strings, numbers, booleans, and `null`.**
They are sent into the isolated preview at runtime, so no expressions, arrays,
objects, or imported values — put anything richer directly in the body markup,
where full Svelte is available. One invalid value rejects the whole `args`
object, so keep every value literal.

### `[example]` — a frozen showcase

Renders **exactly what you wrote**; controls never touch it. Requires a `title`
(unique within the block). Same stage attributes as `[component]` plus
`description`. Examples render below the previews and stay visible on every tab;
the same block also works inside a `[DOC]`, mid-prose.

## Scoped `<script>` / `<style>` — the ladder

Any container can open with a `<script>` and close with a `<style>`; scopes nest
lexically: **file → entity → block**. File script visible everywhere; entity
script (right after the opener) visible to that entity's blocks/body; block
script (the **first** content of the body, `<style>` the **last**) local to that
block. Don't re-import or re-declare a name the file script provides (scopes
nest, they don't shadow); `args` is in scope in preview scripts; reserved names
(`args`, `__sdocsRef`, `__sdocsExample`) are diagnosed where they'd collide.

## `[DOC]` — freeform markdown

Body is markdown, rendered with an auto table of contents (from `##`–`####`
headings; hide with `toc="false"`). Attributes: `title`, `maxWidth`, `padding`,
`contentX`, `toc`, `slug`, `hide`. A leading `#` heading becomes the displayed
page title (the `title` attribute then only names the sidebar entry).

The markdown dialect is GitHub-flavored, plus two Svelte conveniences and inert
fences:

- **`{expression}` interpolation** — values from the file `<script>` drop into
  prose: `currently {version}`. A balanced `{…}` is passed to Svelte verbatim.
- **Svelte islands** — a line starting with a component/HTML tag (`<Button`,
  `<div`) or a Svelte block (`{#snippet`, `{@render`), after a blank line, begins
  an island that runs until its tags/blocks balance. Islands run in the **docs**
  context (structure the page itself; for product-styled output use `[example]`).
- **Snippets** — declare `{#snippet name(...)}…{/snippet}` as an island, render
  with `{@render name(...)}` anywhere in the body.
- **GFM** — headings, links (external open in a new tab), images, tables with
  `:---:` alignment, task lists (`- [x]`), `~~strikethrough~~`, blockquotes,
  rules, and **alerts**: a blockquote whose first line is `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`,
  `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]`, or `[!CAUTION]` renders as a tinted callout.
- **Inert fences** — code inside ``` fences ``` (and `` `inline code` ``) is
  displayed/highlighted, never executed, even if it looks like a component or an
  `[example]` opener. Fence languages: anything shiki knows, plus `sdoc`. Escape
  a literal brace in prose as `\{`.

Drop an `[example]` block anywhere in the flow to showcase real, project-styled
components mid-prose. A page has no controls or prop extraction — for stateful
component demos reach for a `[SHOWCASE]` or `[LAYOUT]`.

## `[PAGE]` — a Svelte-built page

Body is plain Svelte (components, HTML, snippets, expressions) rendered as a real
page in the **docs** context — no markdown, no toc, no stage tooling. This is how
you build a landing page. Attributes: `title`, `maxWidth`, `padding`, `contentX`,
`slug`, `hide`. There's no automatic heading — `title` names the route/sidebar
entry; the markup is entirely yours.

Sectioning is special for pages: a `@section/`-prefixed title behaves like any
entity, but a **sectionless** title routes at the **site root** —
`title="Welcome"` serves at `/welcome`, listed in no sidebar, reached by links or
as the `home` page. Only `[PAGE]` may be sectionless.

Markdown fences don't exist in a PAGE, so show code with the built-in component:

```svelte
<script lang="ts">
	import { CodeBlock } from 'sdocs/ui';
</script>

<CodeBlock code={source} lang="sdoc" />
```

`sdocs/ui` resolves even in standalone projects (the CLI provides its own copy).

## `[LAYOUT]` — a full-page composition

Body is full Svelte, rendered full-width in an **isolated frame**: the host app's
styles don't leak in — only `config.css` plus the file's own `<style>` apply. No
controls, no prop extraction — just the composition. Attributes: `title`, `slug`,
`hide`, `maxWidth` (default `100%`), `padding` (default `0px`), `background`,
`minHeight`. Not the flex stage attributes — a layout body is flow-root. The
frame fills the viewport height and scrolls when the sketch is taller, so a
full-page composition previews like a real browser window; use a viewport unit
(`height: 100vh` or `minHeight="100vh"`) for full height — `height: 100%`
collapses against the content-height canvas. (Despite the name, unrelated to a
SvelteKit `+layout.svelte` — it *is* a page.)

Layouts can link to each other (and to any sdocs page) with plain anchors —
see "Linking between pages" below — so a multi-screen sketch wires its flows
together: a cart layout's checkout button opens the payment layout.

## Writing components so sdocs documents them well

For every previewed component, sdocs parses the source and extracts its full
public API. What's extracted, and from where:

| Category | Source |
|---|---|
| Props | `interface Props { … }` + `let { … } = $props()` (defaults come from the destructuring) |
| Events | props named `on*` whose type contains `=>` (a non-callback `on*` prop stays a prop) |
| Snippets | props typed `Snippet` or `Snippet<[…]>` (the parameter tuple is preserved) |
| Methods | `export function foo() { … }` |
| States | `export const x = $state(…)` / `$derived(…)` |
| CSS custom properties | `var(--name, default?)` usages in the `<style>` block + `@cssvar` annotations |

Rules that make the tables (and interactive controls) come out right:

- **JSDoc descriptions**: a `/** … */` comment on an interface member, exported
  function, or state becomes its description — hard-wrapped lines are rejoined
  (list items keep their breaks) and inline markdown (`` `code` ``, `**bold**`,
  `*italics*`) renders styled.
- **Select controls** need an **inline union** (`variant?: 'primary' | 'secondary'`);
  a type *alias* (`variant?: Variant`) can't be expanded into a control.
- **Snippets**: for `children` / named snippets to be categorized as snippets
  (not props), declare a **named `interface Props`** — an inline
  `{ children: Snippet }` type is read as a prop.
- **`class` / `...rest` forwarding** (a merged `class` + rest spread on the root
  element) is recognized from the `$props()` destructuring and rendered as chips
  under the props — never as fake required prop rows. When the interface
  `extends` a type (e.g. `HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`), the chip names it.
- **Plain-JS components** get the same extraction through JSDoc: an inline
  `/** @type {{ label?: string }} */` on the `$props()` declaration, or
  `@typedef {Object} Props` + `@property {string} [label] - Description` (the
  bracketed name marks it optional; this form carries descriptions too).
- **CSS custom properties**: every `var(--x, fallback)` in the `<style>` block
  is extracted. The default shown is the root `--x: value` declaration if the
  component sets one, else the `var()` fallback when every use agrees — uses
  that disagree show **Mixed** (hover for the per-property breakdown). Add a
  `@cssvar` annotation in a JSDoc block inside the `<script>` to give a var a
  type and description:
  `@cssvar {color} --bg - Surface background (default: var(--base-0))`.
  Types `color` (colour picker) and `dimension` (number + px) get specialised
  controls; other tokens (`shorthand`, `length`, `string`) fall back to a text
  field. Use a single token in the braces — a union there fails to parse and
  drops the var from the docs. A trailing `(default: …)` in the description
  sets the documented default.
- **Limitations**: untyped `$props()` with no JSDoc extracts names and defaults
  only; non-`on*` callbacks are classified as props; complex or imported types
  show by name only (sdocs doesn't follow imports).

## Linking between pages from a stage

An `<a>` inside any stage (a preview, an example, or a layout body) that
points at another sdocs route navigates the **app**, not the iframe — the
Explorer never re-renders inside the stage. Write the href as the target
page's route, **base-relative** (no leading slash), exactly like stage assets:

```svelte
<a href="guides/flows/payment">Payment</a>

<!-- A button as the link: wrap it in the anchor -->
<a href="components/layouts/auth/sign-up" style="display: block; text-decoration: none;">
	<Button text="Sign up" width="fill" />
</a>
```

The route is the section slug plus the slugified title path — what the URL bar
shows for that page. The stage page carries a `<base href>`, so base-relative
links resolve in dev and under a sub-path deploy alike; a root-absolute
`/guides/…` breaks under a sub-path. External `http(s)` links,
`target="_blank"`, `download`, and same-page `#anchors` keep their native
behaviour.

## Two authoring conventions worth internalising

- **Pass CSS custom properties with Svelte's `--prop="value"` attribute syntax**,
  not a `style` string:
  `<Placeholder text="hi" --bg="var(--info-100)" --fg="var(--info-600)" />`.
- **Stages are flex** — lay content out with the stage attributes (`direction`,
  `gap`, `contentX`, `contentY`, `padding`) rather than wrapping content in your
  own flex `<div>`.

## Full example — a component doc

```sdoc
<script lang="ts">
	import Badge from './Badge.svelte';
</script>

[SHOWCASE title="@components/:Display / Badge" description="A small status **badge** — dot, count, or label."]

	[component component={Badge} args={{ text: 'New', size: 'sm' }}]
		<Badge {...args} />
	[/component]

	[example title="Sizes" direction="row" gap="8px" contentY="middle"]
		<Badge text="xs" size="xs" />
		<Badge text="sm" size="sm" />
		<Badge text="md" size="md" />
	[/example]

	[example title="Coloured" description="Theme with `--bg` / `--fg`."]
		<Badge text="info" --bg="var(--info-100)" --fg="var(--info-600)" />
	[/example]

[/SHOWCASE]
```

## Full example — a config

```js
/** @type {import('sdocs').SdocsConfig} */
export default {
	include: ['./src/lib/**/*.sdoc'],
```
